# CASEs with `line` `readiness`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Readiness and slack** — what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up (ADR-073). When transient support can be withdrawn is a line of its own (ADR-087).

| [CASE-206](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md) v2 | A single flat-foldable degree-4 vertex under a footprint budget: its two folding modes meet only at the flat state, so passing between folded states needs the full flat footprint of 1.866, more than twice what either folded state at 150° takes | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". The minimal toy: one rigid flat-foldable vertex with sector angles 60°, 90°, 120° and 90°, whose configuration space is two folding modes meeting only at the flat state, and a declared resource, the plan area of the smallest convex tray that holds it. Folded states cost 0.75 and 0.875; every switch between them passes the flat state, which costs 1 + √3/2 ≈ 1.866, so the bottleneck budget is 1.866 and the reconfiguration slack 0.991. At a budget of 1.5 the sublevel set cuts each branch near flat and both states are held but neither reaches the other. ([NOTE-1616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1616.md)). A mechanical toy; its organizational reading is an analogy. The construction is the filer's. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
